title: The Creative Act
author: Rick Rubin (with Neil Strauss)
blurb: Rick Rubin, the producer behind records across hip-hop, rock and country, distils decades of work with artists into a book about creativity as a way of being. He argues that everyone is a creator, because simply living and perceiving is a creative act. Ideas, in his view, come from a larger Source, and the artist's job is to stay open and notice them rather than force them. He describes the creative process in phases, from gathering seeds, to playful experimentation, to careful crafting, to letting the work go. Along the way he urges readers to keep a beginner's mind, question inherited rules, serve the work instead of the audience, and treat self-doubt as part of the process. The result is a meditative guide to paying attention and making things that feel true.

lessons.b: Rubin argues that creativity isn't reserved for artists, because anyone who perceives the world and responds to it is already creating.
Ideas are better received than invented, so the creator's job is to stay open and catch what is already flowing around them.
